channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Russia Considers Grain Purchases to Offset Export Disruptions
item.description: Russia’s government is planning a series of measures to support grain producers, include crop procurement, preferential loan extensions and sales subsidies, Interfax reported, citing Agriculture Minister Oksana Lut.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Trump’s Economic Isolation Plan Risks Iran Strikes Across Gulf
item.description: President Donald Trump is betting new sanctions, a naval blockade and ramped-up economic pressure against Iran’s trading partners can accomplish what thousands of bombs and missiles could not: force Tehran to accept a deal to end the war on US terms.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin

item.title: Trade Breakdown Deepens US Canada Rift
item.description: US-Canada trade talks collapsed late Friday, triggering 50% US tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods and a pledge from Prime Minister Mark Carney to retaliate dollar for dollar. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend are Bloomberg White House Correspondent Jeff Mason and Bloomberg Markets and Economic Columnist Jonathan Levin to discuss how the dispute could deepen a lasting rupture between the allies while tariff-driven inflation, rising Treasury yields and the $40 trillion US debt load complicate the administration’s economic message ahead of the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sweden’s Kristersson Cancels Campaign Speech After School Attack
item.description: Sweden’s Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson canceled a campaign speech for next month’s general election after a sword attack at a school left a 17-year-old girl dead and three others injured.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Duxbury

item.title: US Envoy Warns Israel on Syria Base Attack Near Turkish Border
item.description: President Donald Trump’s envoy for Syria and Iraq issued a stern warning after Israel’s recent strike on a long-shuttered military base near the Turkish border, invoking the downing of a Russian jet more than a decade ago that escalated regional tensions.
item.dc:creator: Taylan Bilgic

item.title: Manchester City Financial Rules Verdict Hangs Over UK’s Relations With Emiratis
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces an awkward moment when a commission finally rules on the Premier League club’s legal saga.
item.dc:creator: Alex Dooler and Giles Turner

item.title: Ukraine Drones Strike Samara Oil Refinery, E-Commerce Warehouse
item.description: Russia and Ukraine continued to trade strikes on infrastructure facilities overnight, including Ukrainian drone barrages that hit an oil refinery and a warehouse of a major e-commerce company deep within Russia.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Switzerland’s Big Food Question Keeps Voters Busy at Ballot Box
item.description: Switzerland will soon go to the polls on the issue of food, in yet another test of voters’ appetites to answer big questions at the ballot box.
item.dc:creator: Fabrice Obrist

item.title: Reform UK Feuds Sidetrack Nigel Farage’s Push to Prepare Party to Lead
item.description: Reform UK is struggling to professionalize its insurgency against the British political establishment, with infighting over its direction spilling into the open just as Nigel Farage’s party seeks to convince voters it’s an enduring electoral force.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: US Hits Canada With 50% Tariffs as Carney Vows to Retaliate
item.description: US-Canada trade talks fell apart just before a midnight deadline, with 50% tariffs hitting billions of dollars of Canadian goods and Prime Minister Mark Carney vowing to retaliate in a dispute that looks poised to intensify.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, Alicia Diaz and Thomas Seal

item.title: Trump’s New Midterm Pitch to Voters: Pretend I’m on Ballot
item.description: President Donald Trump tried out a new campaign message on Friday, telling voters in South Carolina to “pretend” he was on the ballot and turn out to back his hand-picked candidate, Senator Darline Graham, in a contentious Republican primary.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Catherine Lucey

item.title: Canada Nears Trump Trade Deal | Balance of Power 8/21/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Canada's former Minister of International Trade Mary Ng, former National Security Advisor to President Trump John Bolton, CSIS Senior Nonresident Scholar Clayton Seigle, Rebelle Communications Founder & CEO Laura Fink, and Stonecourt Capital LP Rick Davis. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anwar’s One-Time Ally Turns Rival With New Malaysia Party
item.description: When Rafizi Ramli married in 2011, Malaysia’s future prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim, hosted a celebration at his home. Fifteen years later, the former allies are now political rivals, with Rafizi setting the groundwork to one day sideline his former benefactor.
item.dc:creator: Netty Ismail and Ram Anand

item.title: Leavitt Says She’ll Return to MAGA Inc. After White House
item.description: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said she will return to MAGA Inc., the president’s super political action committee, when she leaves her post later this month.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Seigle: Squeezing Iran Means Confronting China
item.description: Senior Nonresident Scholar at the Center for Strategic and International Studies Clayton Seigle says a successful US economic pressure campaign against Iran would require confronting China, a major buyer of Iranian energy, potentially putting Washington's "fragile trade war détente" with Beijing at risk. Seigle says tougher pressure could also push energy prices higher if Iran retaliates against shipping or regional infrastructure, with US gasoline prices an important political concern ahead of the midterms. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's 'Balance of Power.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Hopeful' US. Canada Will Reach Deal: Fmr. Trade Official
item.description: Former Canadian Trade Minister Mary Ng says she is hopeful the US and Canada can reach a trade agreement before Friday's deadline, pointing to positive signals from negotiators on both sides. Ng also says Canada should continue diversifying its trade relationships, pointing to opportunities across Asia including Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Indonesia. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's 'Balance of Power.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US and Canada Race Against Clock to Hammer Out Trade Deal
item.description: US and Canadian negotiators haggled Friday over terms of a trade deal that would cut tariffs and retaliatory measures between the two major trading partners, with signs of optimism that a pact would be finalized before a midnight deadline in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Josh Wingrove and Joe Deaux

item.title: Trump Says It Was Bessent’s Choice to Intervene in Bond Market
item.description: President Donald Trump said he did not direct Scott Bessent to intervene in the bond market this week, saying that the Treasury secretary acted on his own authority.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: US Chief Justice Lets Trump Keep Building Ballroom for Now
item.description: US Chief Justice John Roberts said President Donald Trump can keep building his massive new White House ballroom for now, giving the Supreme Court more time to consider a longer-term order allowing continued construction.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: Lula Calls Trump to Resume Talks Over US Tariffs on Brazil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged Donald Trump to resume negotiations over US tariffs on Brazil during a Friday phone call, seeking to soothe relations with Washington ahead of the country’s October election.
item.dc:creator: Simone Iglesias
